cyberattack: Bypassing bot protection or access controls
data.description: For the same CAL-ACCESS filer and session, ordinary requests returned Incapsula unsuccessful-request/challenge pages. Within seconds on May 26, path suffixes resembling PDF, CSS and image assets returned campaign-finance HTML, while a non-asset suffix was still blocked. The responses include real figures, not just successful status codes. All 32 selected detail-page captures were digest-verified; nine returned campaign data, and other captures were blocks or errors. The sequence strongly supports path-dependent anti-bot circumvention. A filtering/application mismatch is a plausible mechanism, but the actual configuration, common requester identity and AI attribution remain unestablished. The data were public disclosures.
data.summary: Archived May 26 CAL-ACCESS requests with PDF/CSS/image-looking path suffixes returned real campaign-finance HTML while nearby normal and non-asset variants were blocked. This strongly supports an anti-bot bypass; AI attribution and requester identity remain unknown.
